# resin-lightweight-charts

**Render [resin](https://github.com/nullarch/resin)'s Pine Script visualization
data on TradingView's own open-source
[lightweight-charts](https://github.com/tradingview/lightweight-charts).**

[resin](https://github.com/nullarch/resin) compiles Pine Script v5/v6 and,
since 0.2.0, captures everything a chart needs — plot styles and per-bar
colors, marker conditions, bar colors, hlines, fills, drawing objects — as
plain data. This adapter maps that data onto lightweight-charts, so the whole
path from a `.pine` file to an interactive chart is:

```js
import { transpile, run } from '@nullarch/resin';
import { renderResinViz } from '@nullarch/resin-lightweight-charts';

const result = transpile(source);
if (!result.ok) throw new Error(result.errors.join('\n'));

const res = run(result, data);                    // data: { open, high, low, close, volume, time }
const { chart, remove } = renderResinViz(container, res, data);
```

A `resin run script.pine --viz out.json` dump works the same way — the adapter
consumes the data shape, not the resin package:

```js
renderResinViz(container, dump.viz, dump.bars);
```

Already have a chart? `applyResinViz(chart, res, data)` adds to it and returns
a handle whose `remove()` tears everything down.

## What renders, faithfully or otherwise

lightweight-charts has four marker shapes and no per-bar background API; Pine
has twelve shapes and `bgcolor`. This table is the honest state of the mapping
— "approx." means it draws, but not pixel-identically to TradingView.

| Pine | Rendering | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `plot` line / stepline / histogram / columns / area | ✅ | stepline via `LineType.WithSteps`; per-bar colors on all of them |
| `plot` linebr / areabr / stepline_diamond / cross / circles | ⚠️ approx. | drawn as their nearest base style |
| `plotshape` | ⚠️ approx. | 12 Pine shapes → 4 LWC glyphs (arrows/circle/square); location, size, per-bar color, text carried |
| `plotchar` | ✅ | the character rides in the marker text |
| `plotarrow` | ⚠️ approx. | direction, color, placement; height scaling not mapped |
| `plotcandle` / `plotbar` | ✅ | candlestick series with per-bar body/wick/border colors |
| `barcolor` | ✅ | per-bar override on the main candles, last call wins |
| `hline` | ✅ | price line with style/width/color (const price only, as in Pine) |
| `bgcolor` | ❌ not yet | LWC has no per-bar background; planned as a custom primitive |
| `fill` | ❌ not yet | planned as a custom primitive (refs and per-bar colors are already in the data) |
| `label` / `line` / `box` / `table` drawings | ❌ not yet | creation log is in the data; planned as custom primitives |
| panes | ✅ | `indicator(overlay=)` and `force_overlay` decide main pane vs sub pane |

The mapping tables live in `src/map/` as pure functions and are unit-tested
against fixtures generated by the real resin (`npm run gen:fixtures` — see
`tests/gen-fixtures.mjs`), so contract drift shows up as a fixture diff, not a
runtime surprise.

## API

- `renderResinViz(container, vizOrRunResult, bars, options?)` → `{ chart, series, remove }`
  — creates the chart (pass LWC options via `options.chart`) and applies the viz.
- `applyResinViz(chart, vizOrRunResult, bars, options?)` → `{ series, remove }`
  — applies onto a chart you own. `options.mainSeries: false` skips the OHLCV
  candlesticks.
- Types: `ResinViz` and friends mirror `RunResult.viz` of `@nullarch/resin`
  structurally — a parsed `--viz` JSON satisfies them.
